land.text: the Republic's land, which stayed sovereign under French and Imperial occupation in the Federated Republic dossier

predecessors.note: Continuous government: Juárez moved north in 1864-65 and returned on 15 July 1867.

land.text: the Imperial holdings (Mexico City, Querétaro, Veracruz) returned in June 1867

capitals.name: Mexico City
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Mexico City'. In December 1914 Carranza's forces evacuated it for Veracruz and Villa and Zapata took it (Mexican Revolution page); no capital move is recorded because the Constitutionalists and the Convention each claimed the state.

correction.text: the whole of Mexico, the 1868 shape, from the restoration of the Republic in July 1867

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1867: Cliopatria's Mexico row begins in 1868, but the Restored Republic begins when 'Juárez entered Mexico City on the morning of July 15' 1867 (infobox: fall of the Second Mexican Empire May 1867; Juárez president 1867-1872). The Federated Republic dossier ends in June 1867 and the Second Mexican Empire dossier in June 1867, so the second half of 1867 needs a keyframe: the 1868 shape stands.

2.004 M km2 against the infobox 1,972,550 km2 (no year given; ratio 1.016): the grid shape includes coastal and border cells. The Restored Republic page lists no territorial change for 1867-1876. Cliopatria gives Mexico the Soconusco (Chiapas 271 of 272 cells) and Quintana Roo.

Seven border and coastal cells are dropped against 1868 (1,770 km2, among them cells at Tecate, Mexicali, Sonoyta, Nogales and two off Quintana Roo); the Mexico-United States border page dates no change in 1877, only the Rio Grande cutting off about 2.4 km2 by 1873. Treated as grid noise; the shape stands.
Three cells (759 km2, off Sinaloa and Quintana Roo) return against 1877: grid noise, no dated event.

A one-cell strip along the US border (21 cells, 5,311 km2, from Sonora east to the Big Bend) leaves the shape against 1880. The page dates the 1884 treaty (middle of the Rio Grande) and the 1889 boundary commission but names no transfer of this size, so the strip is a Cliopatria border alignment, not a loss. 1.995 M km2 against the infobox 1,972,550 km2 (ratio 1.01).

correction.text: the whole of Mexico: the Maderista zone in Chihuahua is a ledger loss and gain, not part of the shape

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts a Maderista zone of 28,831 km2 in Chihuahua (the Maderistas row is 34,589 km2) out of the whole of 1911. The page has Orozco and Villa taking Chihuahua City and Ciudad Juárez, the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez on 21 May 1911 and Díaz's resignation in May 1911, so the zone existed only until May. The corrected shape is the whole country; the ledger's loss (1911) and gain (May 1911) carry the carve.
Back to the full 1.995 M km2 after the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez; Madero 'was inaugurated as president in November 1911'.

correction.text: the whole of Mexico throughout the revolutionary years: no seceding state appears on the pages opened

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1913-1919: Cliopatria has no Mexico shape from 1913 to 1919, the years of the Huerta coup (February 1913), the Constitutionalists, the Convention government and Villa and Zapata in Mexico City (December 1914). The pages name no territory lost to a separate state, so the whole country stands; the factions fight over it as one state. The Mexican Revolution is dated 20 November 1910 to 1 December 1920.
Same shape as 1912; Carranza fled Mexico City after the Plan of Agua Prieta, 'the last successful coup of the revolution'; the revolution is dated to 1 December 1920.
1.995 M km2 for 1922-2023 against the infobox 1,972,550 km2 (ratio 1.01). The Chamizal (1963) and 1970 transfers are far below one cell (260 acres, a few km2); the shape stands.

region.text: the whole country, recovered from the Empire

ledger.note: 15 July 1867: Juárez re-enters Mexico City and the Republic is restored. 'Juárez entered Mexico City on the morning of July 15'; elections were called by a law of 17 August 1867, Juárez 'obtained a majority of the votes' in October and took office on 25 December. The Federated Republic of Mexico and the Second Mexican Empire dossiers both end in June 1867; the government is continuous with the first and the second ends.

region.text: the 2.4 km2 the river's shift cut off, far smaller than one 253 km2 grid cell: an empty region on purpose, so the event moves no land

ledger.note: 1873: the Rio Grande's shift costs Mexico a sliver. 'By 1873, the moving river-center border had cut off approximately 2.4 square kilometers (590 acres) of Mexican territory.' Far below one grid cell. [Repair fx-52 (K09, same defect as the 1970 event): the region was the Rio Grande widened by 5 km, which moved 51 Mexican cells to the United States from 1873 until a later keyframe reset the state, although the sliver is below one cell; the region is now empty (Mexico intersected with the United States) and the compiler keeps the caption and skips the cell move.]

November 1876: the Restored Republic gives way to the Porfiriato. Government forces lost at Huamantla on 15 November, Lerdo fled, and Iglesias 'conceded the presidency to Díaz by the end of 1876'; the page's text has Díaz assuming the presidency on 15 February 1877 while its infobox says 15 February 1876. The Mexico page dates his rule 1876-1911. Same state and colour (rule 2).

region.text: the county of Motozintla in Chiapas

ledger.note: 27 September 1882: the boundary treaty with Guatemala. 'The final boundary treaty was signed in Mexico City on September 27 of 1882' (preliminary agreement, New York, 12 August 1882); Guatemala renounced its rights over Chiapas and 'Mexico received the county of Motozintla'. Demarcation 'was completed in 1899'.

region.text: the Maderista zone in Chihuahua, drawn around Chihuahua City in Cliopatria's 1911 shape

ledger.note: 1911: the Maderistas hold ground in Chihuahua. Cliopatria cuts a 28,831 km2 zone around Chihuahua City out of 1911; the page says only that 'a much greater extent in northern Mexico' rose after 20 November 1910 and that Orozco and Villa 'took Mexicali and Chihuahua City' and won Ciudad Juárez, with no dates or boundaries. Page silent on the month and extent: confidence 1.

21 May 1911: the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez ends the Maderista revolt. 'Díaz would abdicate the presidency along with his vice president'; 'Díaz resigned in May 1911 and went into exile', León de la Barra became interim president. The rebel zone returns to the state (the return is the reading; Cliopatria shows the whole country again in 1912).

region.text: the Chamizal tract at El Paso and Ciudad Juárez

ledger.note: 1963: the Chamizal tract returns to Mexico. 'By a treaty negotiated in 1963, Mexico regained most of this land' (the tract the Rio Grande had cut off at El Paso and Ciudad Juárez); the page dates the treaty, not the hand-over.

region.text: the 1.07 km2 Mexico gave in exchange

ledger.note: 1963: in return Mexico transfers 1.07 km2 (260 acres) to the United States under the same Chamizal treaty.

region.text: the land near Presidio and Hidalgo, Texas: tracts of 650 ha (the Presidio-Ojinaga reach) and 195 ha (the Hidalgo-Reynosa channel), each far smaller than one 253 km2 grid cell: an empty region on purpose, so the event moves no land

ledger.note: 1970: the Boundary Treaty (signed 23 November 1970, in force 18 April 1972). It "transferred an area of Mexican territory to the U.S., near Presidio and Hidalgo, Texas, to build flood control channels" (Mexico-United States border page, the event's earlier source) and settled the outstanding Rio Grande disputes. Boundary Treaty of 1970 page (opened in fx-52): the Presidio-Ojinaga reach moved 1,606.19 acres (650 ha) from the north to the south side of the river and the US acquired 1,969.22 acres (796.92 ha) of agricultural land; a second reach moved a net 252 acres (102 ha) south to north; the Hidalgo-Reynosa flood-control channel moved 481.68 acres (194.93 ha) from Mexico to the United States 'in exchange for the transfer from the United States to Mexico of other land' (five parcels near Presidio, the Horcon Tract and Beaver Island, 481.68 acres). The page gives acres and hectares only. [Repair fx-52 (K09), as fx-42 R148 did for the 2009 event: the region was the Rio Grande widened by 5 km, which moved 51 Mexican cells (Coahuila 18, Chihuahua 17, Tamaulipas 15, Nuevo Leon 1) to the United States from 1970 to the 2024 keyframe, although every tract on the page is a few km2, below one cell. The region is now empty (Mexico intersected with the United States): the compiler keeps the caption and skips the cell move; the validator shows a 'region resolves to no cells' warning by design.]

region.text: six islands in the Rio Grande, each far smaller than one 253 km2 grid cell: an empty region on purpose, so the event moves no land

ledger.note: 24 November 2009: 'the U.S. ceded 6 islands in the Rio Grande to Mexico'; 'At the same time, Mexico ceded 3 islands and 2 bancos to the U.S.'; 'the first application of Article III of the 1970 Boundary Treaty' (Mexico-United States border page, which gives no area for the islands). [Repair fx-42, 2 Nov 2026 (dossier request R148): the region was the Rio Grande widened by 5 km, which gave Mexico 96 United States cells (New Mexico 44, Texas 34, Colorado 14) although the river runs wholly inside the United States above El Paso. Six river islands are far smaller than one cell, so the region is now empty (Mexico intersected with the United States): the compiler keeps the caption and skips the cell move. p2000-p2009 events/1 and p2020-p2029 events/3, which hand the strip back, now find nothing to move.]

wars.name: Mexican Revolution

zones.text: Chihuahua, where Orozco and Villa rose in 1910-1911: the Maderista zone of 1911

wars.outcome: The revolt that began on 20 November 1910 ended the Díaz presidency (resignation May 1911, Treaty of Ciudad Juárez 21 May 1911); Huerta's coup of February 1913 led to the Constitutionalist and Convention phases, the constitution of 5 February 1917 and the end of the revolution (1 December 1920 on the page). No territory changed hands between states.
wars.note: Cliopatria's only rebel row is the Maderistas of 1911; the later factions (Huerta, Constitutionalists, Villa, Zapata, the Convention) are not rows and the pages name no zones for them.

certainty.note: Frontiers with the United States run along the Rio Grande and the 1848/1853 lines, but the Guatemalan border is unsettled until the treaty of 27 September 1882 and the Yucatán interior is not controlled (Caste War, page).

The Guatemalan frontier is sharp from the 1882 treaty (demarcation completed 1899) and the US frontier from the 1884 treaty on the Rio Grande (the middle of the river, regardless of channel changes); Quintana Roo and the Belize frontier are not covered by the pages opened and stay as Cliopatria draws them.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Mexico' row (1868-2024, Wikidata Q5062192) shares its Wikidata id with centralist-mexico (the Centralist Republic of 1835-1846, am-08-e/-g). They are different regimes of one country: the Cliopatria 'Mexico' row is the federal republic from the Restored Republic on and is the continuation of federated-republic-of-mexico (1823-1867, ends June 1867, successor mexico). One dossier here under the slug mexico; the Q5062192 id is the Centralist Republic's and should not be used for the state page link without checking. The family americas matches the Federated and Centralist dossiers: one hue. Gaps: (1) Cliopatria has no Mexico shape for 1913-1919: a new keyframe holds the whole country. (2) 1867 (second half) is a new keyframe; Cliopatria's row starts in 1868. (3) The seven-cell, three-cell and 21-cell changes of 1877, 1880 and 1890 are border and coastal grid noise, no page dates them. (4) The Mexican Revolution's factions after 1911 are not rows; their zones are unnamed in the pages. (5) Not opened (page budget 5 of 5): the Belize-Mexico border (Treaty of 1893, Quintana Roo, Chan Santa Cruz until 1901), Clipperton Island (1931 arbitration), the Cristero War, the 1933 Rio Grande rectification (equal areas exchanged 1935-1938). Names for the gazetteer: place 'Motozintla' (Chiapas, about -92.25, 15.37). The rulers strip is omitted: the pages give only Juárez and Lerdo (1867-1876) and Díaz's span. Counterpart 'maderistas' is another part's dossier.
Fix pass fx-42 (2 Nov 2026), dossier request R148: ledger/9 (24 November 2009, six Rio Grande islands) moves no land; the Rio Grande plus 5 km region it had took 96 United States cells.
